rationale: This is a mechanical rank-difference of two long-published anomalies (R&D/advertising intensity and the Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan net-external-financing effect) with no conditioning structure, so any result is a near-certain rediscovery of their additive combination rather than evidence of a funding-source mechanism.

Conditioning the debt-versus-equity issuance mix on R&D intensity is a genuinely interactive and economically motivated idea, but the construction is fragile — it depends on IND_RANK being non-negative (a centered rank would flip the sign for low-R&D firms) and the un-winsorized ZSCORE of (dltis−sstk)/at will let a handful of levered issuers dominate the spread.

In raw (unranked) levels the financing flows are an order of magnitude larger and more volatile than xrd/at, so the signal will be dominated by net payout/external financing and collapses into the known financing and net-payout-yield anomalies while also duplicating proposal 1.

The expression is internally consistent (product of non-negative ranks, negative expected sign) and the financed-acquirer story is coherent, but both legs are individually established negative predictors (asset/intangible growth and gross issuance), so it risks being an amplified rediscovery of stock-financed-acquirer underperformance rather than a new interaction.

GROWTH of sale divided by three-year cumulative R&D is dominated by sales growth (not research productivity) and explodes for near-zero R&D firms with no COALESCE guard, so the signal is effectively issuance × sales growth — a combination whose natural direction (glamour issuers underperforming) contradicts the stated positive sign.

A rank difference between R&D intensity and multi-year share-count growth is simply the sum of two of the best-documented anomalies (R&D-to-assets and net share issuance/Pontiff-Woodgate), and it is also largely redundant with proposal 1 in this same batch.
